x: Bryan came all the way from Eastleigh to run in the 2 miles, which is enthusiasm indeed.

Bryan, who had come all the way from Southampton to run in this race. He very sportingly agreed to turn out in the 1 mile, which was later in the programme, and immediately his race was over, he left to catch his return train home, and so was at the meeting about half an hour only, and yet was willi…
Also quite a number of our lads were unable to turn out, and as these included Broadbent, Dumbrill, Jarlett, Watts, Carter, Smart, also Bryan, of Eastleigh, the South team was very much weakened.

The race was a " carve up " from the commencement between Bingham, Bryan and Carter ; all three hanging on, and it was very obvious in the second lap that Bryan, who was forcing the pace, had the measure of the other two.

5, Carter (47.49) ; 11, Bryan (48.42) ; 12, Herbert (R.A.F.) (48.46) ; 13, Patience (Armv) (48.53) ; and 22, Cohen (50.8). International Race, at Belfast, on March 21st, over 6½ miles. 35 teams, 315 competitors.

The course was one of two laps, and first time round the leading bunch included Carter, Dan Patience, Draper and Bryan. With about a mile to go Tom Carter was leading Dan by about 30 yards, with Draper about the same distance behind, and Bryan fourth.

Bryan taking fourth place for the South, and Harry Shields also showed a big improvement on his previous running this season. Also held in conjunction with the meeting was a R.W.A. 5 Miles Road Walk Handicap, which started and finished on the track.

The finish saw Herbert in front clocking 42.42; Hoath 2nd, 42.49; Carter 4th, 43.3; Tobin 15th, 44.44; Bryan 17th, 44.49; Cohen 18th, 45.4; Peck 21st, 45.15; Shields 25th, 45.34; Morrell 40th, 47.16; Spencer 55th, 49.25; White 63rd, 50.39 and Jannaway 70th, 53.30.
